Can Indian homegrown smartphone brands compete with global giants? | Photo Credit: Reuters
India’s IT Minister, Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a recent interaction with NDTV , outlined an ambitious target that by October 23, 2028, India will have its own mobile phone brand, designed and made locally. While the minister’s intent reflects a strong government policy to foster indigenous manufacturing and self-reliance, translating that vision into commercial success presents steep operational and market hurdles.
The competitive landscape is daunting as Chinese Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) control nearly 70% of India’s smartphone market, as per Counterpoint. Apple, on the other side of the globe, dominates premium market phones. The iPhone maker’s dominance has forced Chinese players to re-evaluate their strategies across price bands.
